title: constraint_model.ipynb

canonical_node.axiom: A strategy is admissible only if it satisfies all six constraints: justice, mercy, freewill, love, entropy, and holiness.
definitions: Constraint function: a function taking a strategy parameter vector and returning True/False based on threshold conditions.

Strategy parameter vector: a 10-dimensional vector with components payment_magnitude, cost_to_sinner, coercion_level, relational_access, negentropy_input, corruption_addressed, voluntary_by_redeemer, scope, permanence, source_is_external.
All-passed boolean: a flag indicating that all six constraint functions return True for a given parameter vector.
Cross configuration: the parameter vector corresponding to an external voluntary substitute, full payment, zero coercion, full access, full negentropy, full corruption resolution.
derivation: Define six constraint functions with threshold conditions on the parameter vector.
Evaluate any strategy by checking all six constraints; the strategy passes if all return True.
Perform grid and random search over the parameter space to find all-passing configurations.
Verify that the only all-passing configuration found is the cross configuration.
canonical_node.action: Given a strategy parameter vector, evaluate all six constraints and return the constraint count and all-passed boolean. Use optimization to search for all-passing configurations.
boundary: Does not define the specific threshold values for each constraint.
Does not apply the model to specific biblical strategies; that is the role of test09_constraint_satisfaction.ipynb.
Does not extend to 100,000 random trials; that is the role of free_body_model.ipynb.
test: For any parameter vector, the constraint functions return deterministic True/False.
The optimization search covers the full continuous parameter space and finds no all-passing configuration other than the cross configuration.
The Monte Carlo variant in free_body_model.ipynb uses the same constraint functions and reproduces the uniqueness result.

dg1_dependencies: None explicitly stated; the notebook defines the constraint functions from scratch.
dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a reusable constraint satisfaction engine for evaluating strategies against six constraints.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the ability to evaluate any strategy deterministically against the six constraints.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: Without this model, the formal test (test09) and the Monte Carlo extension (free_body_model) would lack the constraint functions and evaluation framework.

overstatement_risks: The document claims exhaustive search verifies uniqueness, but the search method (grid/random) may not be truly exhaustive over continuous space.
The threshold values for constraints are not specified, so the model's behavior is not fully reproducible without the notebook code.
kill_conditions: If the constraint functions are not deterministic or not well-defined.
If the optimization search is not actually exhaustive or misses solutions.
risk.lean_target: Formalize the constraint functions and thresholds in a verifiable form.

plain_summary: This notebook defines a constraint satisfaction engine with six constraints and a 10-parameter strategy space. It claims to verify that only the cross configuration satisfies all constraints, but the proof relies on search methods and lacks explicit thresholds.
